Operator: Good day, and welcome to the TeleMedia Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing and using your microphone will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to TeleMedia Corp's Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Lopez, Chief Network Officer; David Chen, Chief Commercial Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Operating Officer; and other members of our leadership team. Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3, demonstrating our continued commitment to growth and innovation. Our success is driven by our dedicated team and strategic investments. We've seen impressive net subscriber additions across residential and business segments, robust EBITDA margin expansion, sustainable dividend growth supporting shareholder returns, accelerated 5G network investments, optimized spectrum utilization, strong content and media performance, positive ARPU trends from pricing and bundling, and meaningful enterprise B2B wins. The launch of TeleStream Plus is exceeding expectations, resulting in higher engagement and revenue uplift. Further milestones include expanded fiber overbuilds and 5G fixed wireless access trials. We are also focusing on cybersecurity enhancements and AI-driven efficiencies. Our dedication to customer experience improvements is bearing fruit through lower churn. Our strategy is to enhance converged services offerings. We are actively investing in edge computing and Open RAN. We are also exploring private network opportunities and finally, analyzing regulatory impacts on spectrum auctions.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Alex. Now, let's review our financial performance. Revenue for the quarter reached $6.20 billion, reflecting a 6% increase year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA was $2.18 billion, resulting in a margin of 35.2%. We maintain a disciplined approach to cost management and capital allocation. Capital expenditures totaled $1.8 billion, primarily allocated to expanding our 5G network, fiber infrastructure, and content investments.

Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Moving to our subscriber metrics, which remain a cornerstone of our growth story in this competitive telecom and media landscape. I'm pleased to report that in Q3, we delivered total net subscriber additions of 285,000 revenue-generating units, or RGUs, across our residential and business segments. This marks a 12% year-over-year increase from 255,000 in Q3 last year, and sequentially up 8% from Q2's 265,000. These results underscore the strength of our hybrid fiber-coaxial network investments and our aggressive push into converged services, even as we navigate macroeconomic headwinds like inflation impacting consumer spending.

Let me break this down by segment, starting with residential, which accounted for 78% of our net adds this quarter. Residential net subscriber additions came in at 225,000 RGUs, a robust 15% YoY increase and our strongest quarter since Q4 2022. Broadband drove the lion's share at 150,000 net adds—up 18% YoY—fueled by our ongoing FTTH overbuilds, where we've now passed 2.5 million homes with gigabit symmetrical speeds. Penetration in these footprints hit 42%, ahead of our 40% target, thanks to promotional pricing on our 2 Gbps tiers, which saw take-rates exceed 25%. Video net adds were solid at 45,000, with churn dipping to a record-low 1.1% monthly rate, bolstered by our "X1 Stream" bundle integrating linear TV with ad-supported FAST channels from partners like Tubi and Pluto TV—mirroring strategies we've seen succeed at peers like Comcast's Xfinity.

Mobile rounded out residential at 30,000 net adds, a 10% YoY uptick, primarily from 5G fixed wireless access trials in rural overlays, where we're leveraging C-band spectrum acquired in the 2021 FCC auction to compete with T-Mobile's FWA momentum. Regionally, the Northeast U.S. was our powerhouse at 120,000 net adds, driven by dense urban fiber densification in markets like Boston and Philly. The Midwest contributed 60,000, up 25% YoY on greenfield FTTH builds in partnership with homebuilders, while our Latin American footprint—via our JV with Claro in Mexico—added 25,000, offsetting softer demand in Brazil amid economic volatility. Overall residential ARPU grew 3% YoY to $128, reflecting successful upselling to multi-play bundles amid cord-cutting pressures; U.S. pay-TV households continue to decline industry-wide at 4-5% annually, per Nielsen data, but our video retention held firm.

Shifting to business, we posted 60,000 net subscriber additions, up 20% YoY and 15% sequentially—a testament to our enterprise pivot. This segment now represents 22% of total RGUs, with ARPU at $450 monthly, more than 3x residential. Ethernet and fiber services led with 35,000 net adds, propelled by SD-WAN deployments for mid-market SMBs—we've activated over 10,000 sites YTD on our "TeleMedia Edge" platform, which integrates with Cisco's Viptela for zero-touch provisioning. Our 5G private networks for manufacturing clients added 15,000, including a landmark deal with a Fortune 500 automaker in the Southeast U.S. for edge computing at their EV plants, tapping into the same industrial IoT tailwinds boosting Verizon's enterprise growth.

Regionally, U.S. business was stellar at 45,000 net adds, with the Southeast surging 30% YoY on data center proximity plays near hyperscalers like AWS in Virginia. Internationally, Europe contributed 10,000 via our Vodafone alliance in the UK and Germany, where we're co-investing in open RAN to cut capex by 20%. Churn here remains elite at 0.8% annually, well below the industry average of 1.5% per Infonetics Research, due to sticky multi-year contracts with SLAs guaranteeing 99.999% uptime.

Strategically, these results validate our "Converged Growth 2025" initiative: $4.2 billion in capex this year, with 60% allocated to network hardening—including DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades to 10 Gbps in 40% of our footprint by year-end—and the rest to M&A tuck-ins like our recent $800 million acquisition of a regional fiber provider in the Sunbelt. We're also leaning into media synergies, cross-promoting our ad inventory across 15 million residential subs to streamers like Netflix and Disney+, which boosted video attach rates by 5 points.

Looking forward, we guide to Q4 residential net adds of 210,000-240,000 and business at 55,000-65,000, implying total RGUs of 270,000-300,000. Risks include competitive pricing from cable peers like Charter and wireless carriers' FWA expansion, but our fiber advantage and low churn position us for sustained 10-12% YoY growth through 2025.

Good afternoon, everyone. Today, I'd like to dive deep into our EBITDA margin performance, which came in at 35.2% for the quarter—up 320 basis points year-over-year from 32.0% in Q3 last year, and 110 basis points sequentially from Q2's 34.1%. This marks our strongest quarterly margin in the past five years and puts us ahead of the Telecom/Media peer average of around 31% as reported by consensus estimates from Bloomberg and FactSet.

Let me break this down by the key drivers and trends shaping our margin profile. First, revenue mix shift toward high-margin segments was the primary upside driver, contributing +450 bps YoY impact. Wireless services, which now represent 52% of total revenue—up from 48% a year ago—delivered an industry-leading blended ARPU of $58.70, a 4.2% YoY increase driven by 5G premium plan adoption. Over 65% of our postpaid subscribers are now on 5G Unlimited plans, similar to what we've seen at peers like Verizon with their myPlan offerings, generating 25-30% higher ARPU than legacy 4G tiers.

Broadband and fiber segments contributed another +200 bps, with fixed wireless access volumes surging 28% YoY to 1.2 million subscribers, leveraging our C-band spectrum assets for gigabit speeds at lower capex intensity than traditional FTTH. This mirrors T-Mobile's FWA success, where margins exceed 45%. On the media side, our streaming JV with Paramount Global—branded as 'TeleStream Plus'—hit 18 million paid subs, up 22% YoY, with direct-to-consumer revenue growing 35% and boasting 50%+ EBITDA margins due to ad-tier bundling and lower churn at 4.1% monthly.

Regionally, U.S. operations drove 70% of the mix benefit, with margins at 38%, while EMEA lagged at 28% due to regulatory price caps in the EU—think Ofcom-style interventions—but we offset this with 15% YoY growth in enterprise 5G private networks for IoT applications.

Second, opex efficiencies and digital transformation added +280 bps YoY impact. Cost discipline was our margin accelerator. SG&A as a percentage of revenue fell to 18.2% from 20.1%, saving $120 million YoY, primarily from AI-powered network operations center automation. We've virtualized 72% of our core network using Open RAN and cloud-native architectures—partnering with Ericsson and Nokia—reducing opex by 22% per cell site versus legacy hardware. This is ahead of AT&T's trajectory and positions us for sub-10% annual opex growth through 2025.

Content costs, a perennial pressure point in Media, were managed to just +3% YoY growth despite $450 million in sports rights amortization for NFL and Premier League packages. We achieved this via output deals with studios like Warner Bros. Discovery and savvy NFL Sunday Ticket integrations post-Fox merger dynamics, keeping content opex at 12% of media revenue versus Netflix's 65% gross margin squeeze.

Offset by strategic investments, which created a -410 bps YoY headwind. Network expansion capex intensity rose to 14.5% of revenue from 13.2%, reflecting $900 million invested in 5G Standalone core upgrades and edge computing for low-latency media delivery—critical for our 8K streaming trials and cloud gaming partnerships with Microsoft Azure. Spectrum renewal fees in Asia-Pacific, where we hold 15% market share via our Singtel JV, added $50 million in non-recurring costs amid 6GHz auction pressures similar to the U.S. FCC's ongoing debates. Churn ticked up 20 bps to 1.05% in wireless due to competitive promotions from Dish Network's Boost Infinite, but our loyalty programs capped the margin drag.

Looking at trends, our trailing 12-month EBITDA margin has expanded 410 bps to 34.8%, outpacing Comcast's 28% and Charter's 32% amid cord-cutting headwinds. We've seen consistent +100 bps quarterly gains since Q1 2023, driven by scale in 5G now covering 95% of our U.S. footprint and media synergies post our 2022 acquisition of a regional content aggregator akin to fuboTV.

Strategically, we're targeting 37-39% margins by FY2025 through 5G monetization via network slicing for enterprise AR/VR media applications, projecting +$500 million in high-margin revenue; AI and automation with $200 million in FY24 capex for generative AI customer service, aiming to cut call center costs 30% like Vodafone's initiatives; regional tailwinds like U.S. fiber overbuild acceleration to 55% coverage, countering EU margin compression via M&A in deregulated markets like Poland; and media efficiency by bundling TeleStream with wireless at 20% discounts, mirroring Disney+'s Hulu bundle success, to boost attach rates to 40%.

Good afternoon, everyone. As your CFO, I'm pleased to dive into our dividend sustainability and overall shareholder returns, a cornerstone of our capital allocation strategy in this dynamic Telecom and Media landscape. We've built a reputation for delivering reliable, growing returns to shareholders, even amidst the seismic shifts from 5G monetization, fiber overbuilds, streaming cord-cutting, and spectrum auctions.

First, a snapshot of our current dividend profile. We declared a quarterly dividend of $0.67 per share earlier this month, marking a 3% increase year-over-year and our 18th consecutive quarter of growth. This translates to an annualized dividend of $2.68 per share, yielding approximately 5.4% based on yesterday's close of $49.60. For context, this comfortably outpaces the S&P 500 Communications Services sector average yield of 3.2% and peers like AT&T at 5.1% or Verizon at 6.8%, while maintaining superior coverage metrics.

Sustainability starts with robust free cash flow generation—our North Star metric. In Q3, we generated $2.4 billion in FCF, up 12% year-over-year, driven by wireless service revenue growth of 4.2% to $8.7 billion and broadband ARPU expansion of 2.8% to $68 in our U.S. fixed-line segment. Full-year 2024 FCF guidance remains firmly at $9.5 billion to $10 billion, reflecting disciplined capex at 16% of revenue—down from 18% last year as our 5G Standalone core network rollout matures. Our dividend consumes just $1.9 billion annually, providing a healthy FCF payout ratio of 65% on a trailing twelve-month basis, with coverage exceeding 1.8x even under conservative stress scenarios like a 10% ARPU headwind from promotional pricing.

Leverage is another pillar. Net debt stands at $85 billion, with a net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA ratio of 2.6x—well within our 2.5x-3.0x target band and below Verizon's 2.8x or Comcast's 3.1x. We've proactively managed this through $1.2 billion in pension contributions and $500 million in hybrid bond redemptions this quarter, bolstering our investment-grade ratings across all three agencies. Moody's recently affirmed our Baa1 stable outlook, citing our "resilient dividend framework amid media volatility."

Turning to trends, our dividend has compounded at a 4% CAGR over the past five years, from $2.28 in 2019 to today's $2.68, outpacing inflation and matching our mid-single-digit EPS growth. This resilience shines through industry headwinds: linear TV ad revenue declined 8% industry-wide per Magna Global data, yet our hybrid model—blending Verizon-like wireless with Disney-esque streaming—delivered 15% EBITDA growth to $4.1 billion in Q3. We've offset pay-TV subscriber losses of 450k primarily legacy cable with 1.2 million net adds to our TeleStream+ streaming platform, now at 28 million subs with 92% domestic retention and ARPU of $14.50, fueled by ad-tier uptake akin to Netflix's successful pivot.

Regionally, our U.S. operations anchor sustainability, contributing 72% of FCF with 5G penetration at 68% post our C-band spectrum deployment—mirroring T-Mobile's edge but with higher enterprise mix 25% of wireless revenue from 5G fixed wireless access. In Europe, our Vodafone JV in Germany and Italy generated €1.1 billion in FCF, supporting a €0.45/share regional payout with 2.1x coverage, despite regulatory pressures on roaming fees. Asia-Pacific, via our Singtel stake and Indonesian tower assets, added $300 million in distributable cash, bolstered by 4G/5G upgrades amid Indonesia's 270 million mobile subs market. Latin America remains a growth wildcard: our Claro Brazil media arm saw 22% YoY digital ad growth, cushioning FX volatility.

Shareholder returns extend beyond dividends via our $5 billion share repurchase authorization, of which we've deployed $1.8 billion YTD at an average price of $47.20—about 8% below current levels. This opportunistic buyback, paired with the dividend, delivers a total shareholder yield of 9.2% trailing twelve months, topping Comcast's 4.5% and the sector's 6.1%. Since our 2021 convergence strategy—acquiring streamer assets for $12 billion—we've returned $18.4 billion to shareholders, including $12.7 billion in dividends and $5.7 billion in buybacks, while growing book value per share 11%.

Strategically, sustainability hinges on three initiatives. One: Capex efficiency. Our Open RAN trials with Nokia and Samsung reduced 5G opex by 15% in pilot markets, with full-scale rollout targeting $1 billion in savings by 2026—freeing FCF for returns. Two: Synergies from M&A. Post our $4.5 billion fiber acquisition in the U.S. Southeast mirroring Frontier's model, we've realized $250 million in annual cost savings, expanding gigabit coverage to 55% of homes passed and boosting broadband FCF margins to 42%. Three: Media diversification. With linear TV comprising just 18% of revenue down from 32% in 2020, our 5G-enabled edge computing for live sports streaming—partnered with the NFL and akin to DAZN's playbook—projects 20% CAGR in digital video revenue through 2027.

Looking ahead, we're confident in sustaining and growing returns. We guide to 3-5% dividend growth in 2025, supported by $10.5-$11 billion FCF, assuming mid-single-digit wireless EBITDA growth and streaming subs hitting 32 million. Payout ratio targets remain 60-70% of FCF, with leverage at 2.7x. In a downside case—say, delayed 3.5GHz spectrum auctions or 5% churn spike from economic slowdown—coverage stays above 1.5x, validated by our annual dividend stress test.

Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Moving now to our network investments, which remain the cornerstone of our long-term growth strategy here at TeleMedia Corp. As you know, we're aggressively advancing our 5G Standalone—SA—deployment while optimizing our capital expenditure, or CapEx, to deliver superior network economics and unlock new revenue streams in media and entertainment.

First, on CapEx: For Q3, we deployed $1.8 billion in total network CapEx, representing about 28% of our quarterly revenue and in line with our full-year guidance of $7.2 to $7.5 billion. Of that, 5G-related investments accounted for $1.1 billion, or roughly 61% of the total—a slight uptick from 58% in Q2 as we accelerated mid-band C-band deployments. This includes $450 million on radio access network—RAN—hardware, $350 million on transport and fiber backhaul, and $300 million on core network upgrades and edge computing facilities. Year-to-date, our cumulative 5G CapEx stands at $3.1 billion, putting us on track for the high end of our $4.8 to $5.0 billion annual target for next-gen networks.

Now, turning to deployment progress: We're making exceptional strides in 5G coverage and capacity. As of quarter-end, our Non-Standalone—NSA—5G footprint covers 92% of our U.S. postpaid customer base, up from 87% last quarter, with aggregate 5G traffic now comprising 68% of our total mobile data usage—a 15 percentage point increase year-over-year. More importantly, we've hit a major milestone with Standalone 5G: 45% population coverage in our top 50 U.S. markets, including full SA rollout in 22 major metros like New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago. This is powered by our recent $2.5 billion C-band spectrum acquisition in the FCC Auction 107, where we secured 280 MHz of premium mid-band spectrum—ideal for balancing coverage and capacity.

Technically, we're leveraging Massive MIMO 64T64R configurations from our Ericsson and Nokia partnerships, achieving peak downlink speeds exceeding 2 Gbps in tested markets. We've also initiated Open RAN trials in three regions, integrating DISH Network-inspired architectures to reduce vendor lock-in and target 20-25% RAN CapEx savings by 2025. On the transport side, we've deployed 15,000 miles of new dark fiber in partnership with Zayo Group, ensuring low-latency backhaul for our 5G edge nodes—critical for media applications like AR/VR streaming and cloud gaming, where we've seen latency drop to under 10ms in pilot tests with our TeleStream OTT platform.

Regionally, our U.S. operations lead the pack: 5G SA now serves 75 million pops, with CapEx efficiency improving to $120 per covered pop, down 12% from last year thanks to site densification and AI-driven optimization via our Amdocs OSS stack. In Europe, post our Vodafone joint venture in Germany and the UK, we've achieved 65% NSA coverage across 120 million pops, but spectrum harmonization delays from recent EU auctions have pushed $200 million of CapEx into Q4. We're mitigating this with dynamic spectrum sharing—DSS—between 4G LTE and 5G NR. In Latin America, our Claro Brasil subsidiary hit 55% coverage in São Paulo and Rio, investing $250 million YTD amid favorable mmWave auctions, where we're targeting fixed wireless access—FWA—for underserved media markets.

Strategically, these investments are yielding strong returns. Our 5G ARPU premium has expanded to $8 per month for SA users, driven by bundled media services—think unlimited TeleStream 8K streaming and low-latency esports. We've observed a 22% uplift in data consumption among 5G users, directly fueling our edge content delivery network—CDN—synergies, where 5G offload now handles 35% of our video traffic, reducing peering costs by 18%. Looking ahead, we expect CapEx intensity to peak at 22% of revenue in 2024 before tapering to 18% by 2026 as 5G matures and we shift toward OpEx-light models like network slicing for enterprise 5G private networks. Supply chain headwinds from Huawei restrictions and chip shortages have added 5-7% to costs, but our diversified supplier base—Nokia, Samsung, and emerging players like Mavenir—positions us well.

Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Before we move on, I'd like to dive deeper into one of our key strategic assets: our spectrum portfolio. As many of you know, spectrum is the lifeblood of our wireless operations here at TeleMedia Corp, powering everything from our nationwide 5G network to our growing fixed wireless access offerings and media delivery services. Today, I'll cover our current utilization rates, year-over-year trends, and our forward-looking allocation plans, with a focus on how we're optimizing this asset to drive both top-line growth and margin expansion.

First, a quick snapshot of our holdings. We control approximately 425 MHz of average spectrum depth across our 320 million POPs footprint—ranking us competitively with peers like Verizon and T-Mobile. This includes a balanced mix: about 140 MHz in low-band sub-1 GHz assets for coverage, 200 MHz in premium mid-band C-band and 2.5 GHz for capacity, and 85 MHz in high-band mmWave for ultra-high-speed pockets. We've methodically built this portfolio through FCC auctions—like our $2.8 billion spend in the 2021 C-band auction, where we secured 100 MHz nationwide—and strategic acquisitions, including the $1.2 billion tuck-in deal for Dish's AWS-3 spectrum last year.

Now, turning to utilization. Our overall network spectrum utilization stands at 68% as of Q3 2024, up from 58% a year ago and 52% two years back. This reflects the explosive data growth we've seen—our total wireless data traffic surged 42% YoY to 15 EB quarterly, driven by 5G smartphone penetration now at 62% of our postpaid base and the ramp in FWA subscribers, which hit 1.2 million, up 180% YoY. Breaking it down by band:

Low-band 600 MHz and 850 MHz: Utilization at 55%, providing rock-solid coverage for 98% of Americans. We've seen slower uptake here due to its role as an anchor layer, but it's critical for rural expansion. In regions like the Midwest and Southeast—think our partnerships with agricultural IoT providers in Iowa and Kansas—low-band utilization is pushing 65%, supporting precision farming apps with median latencies under 40 ms.

Mid-band C-band 3.7-3.98 GHz and 2.5 GHz: This is our crown jewel, at 82% utilization overall. C-band alone is at 78%, with speeds averaging 450 Mbps download. Urban markets like New York, LA, and Chicago are fully loaded at 90-95%, where we're handling 5G SA traffic for enterprise customers—think private 5G networks for stadiums like MetLife and SoFi, in collaboration with Ericsson. Our media division is leveraging this for low-latency content delivery; for instance, we've cut buffering on our TeleMedia Stream service by 35% during live events like NFL games, boosting average watch time by 22%.

mmWave 28 GHz and 39 GHz: Utilization here is at 45%, more measured due to its short range, but throughput is stellar at 1.2 Gbps peak. We're concentrating it in high-density venues—airports, arenas, and enterprise campuses—covering 15 major metros. Events like Coachella and CES this year saw 2x traffic spikes, with no degradation thanks to our dynamic spectrum sharing pilots using CBRS Band 48.

Regionally, utilization varies predictably: Northeast and West Coast metros average 75%, fueled by business ARPU at $85/month from 5G fixed services. Sunbelt markets like Texas and Florida are at 72%, with strong FWA adoption amid housing booms. Rural areas lag at 52%, but that's by design—we're prioritizing capacity where revenue density is highest, with ARPU 40% above national averages in top tiers.

These trends aren't accidental; they're the result of aggressive technical initiatives. We've deployed carrier aggregation across 8-10 layers in 85% of our 5G footprint, boosting effective capacity by 25%. Our Open RAN trials with Nokia and Samsung in Phoenix and Atlanta have reduced integration costs by 18% while maintaining 99.999% uptime. Network slicing is a game-changer for media—dedicated slices for our TeleMedia+ streaming ensure <10 ms latency for gaming and AR/VR, positioning us against hyperscalers like AWS and Netflix CDNs. And on the efficiency front, AI-driven traffic steering has improved spectral efficiency from 4.2 to 5.1 bits/Hz, directly flowing to our EBITDA margins, which expanded 220 bps to 48% this quarter.

Looking ahead to future allocation plans, we're laser-focused on three pillars: refarming, acquisition, and monetization. Refarming legacy spectrum: Over the next 12-18 months, we'll refarm 40 MHz of our 2G/3G 1900 MHz PCS holdings to 5G NR, targeting a 15% capacity uplift in secondary markets like the Rust Belt. This is low-capex—under $300 million total—and high-ROI, with payback in under a year via reduced churn.

New spectrum acquisition: We're actively bidding in the FCC's upcoming 3.45-3.55 GHz auction, aiming for 60-80 MHz to bolster mid-band depth to 280 MHz average. We've allocated $1.5-2 billion for this and potential CBRS PAL expansions. Internationally, through our 20% stake in a Mexican JV with América Móvil, we're eyeing 3.5 GHz assets to serve cross-border roaming for U.S. expats.

Strategic monetization and allocation: We'll allocate 20% of mid-band capacity to enterprise private networks, targeting $800 million in new revenue by 2025—think manufacturing campuses with Rockwell Automation integrations. For media, 10% of spectrum will go to edge caching nodes, reducing transit costs by 25% and enabling 8K streaming trials. FWA gets a big boost: we're doubling low/mid-band allocation there, projecting 3 million subs by YE24, with $30 ARPU capturing broadband switchers from cable peers like Comcast. Finally, dynamic spectrum access via our Comsearch acquisition will let us opportunistically tap idle TV white space, adding 10-15 MHz equivalent in rural pockets without auctions.

Financially, this translates to disciplined capex: $7.2 billion for FY24, with 55% to spectrum-related RAN upgrades, yielding 3x ROI on 5G investments to date. We're guiding for wireless service revenue growth of 8-10% in '24, with spectrum efficiency driving 2-3 points of that. Compared to peers, our utilization edge—10 points above the industry average per Ookla reports—positions us to outperform on FCF conversion, targeting 18% this year.

Good afternoon, everyone. I'll now dive into the performance of our Content and Media segment, which continues to be a high-growth engine for TeleMedia Corp, leveraging our integrated telco-media ecosystem much like our peers at AT&T post-WarnerMedia merger or Liberty Global's content synergies. This quarter, the segment delivered robust results amid a dynamic landscape of cord-cutting acceleration—U.S. pay-TV households down 5% YoY per Nielsen data—shifting ad dollars to CTV, and intensifying competition from pure-plays like Netflix and Disney+.

Segment revenue reached $2.85 billion in Q3, marking our strongest quarterly performance since launching our flagship TeleStream OTT platform in 2021. This represents 22% of total company revenue, up from 19% a year ago, driven by a healthy mix: Subscription revenue $1.75 billion, +22% YoY, fueled by 1.8 million net paid subscriber adds. Our ad-supported tier, priced at $7.99/month—mirroring Paramount+'s successful model—now accounts for 35% of new sign-ups, boosting penetration without eroding premium ARPU.

Advertising revenue $750 million, +15% YoY, with CTV ad loads up 25% thanks to our proprietary AI-driven dynamic ad insertion tech. We captured 12% more programmatic spend via integrations with The Trade Desk and Google's DV360, capitalizing on the 30% YoY CTV ad market growth per IAB estimates. Content licensing and other $350 million, +10% YoY, including $150 million from syndicating our original IP—think 'TelePrime Originals' like our hit sci-fi series Quantum Edge, akin to Amazon's The Boys—to international AVOD platforms in APAC and LATAM.

Excluding FX impacts, growth was 20% YoY, with U.S. contributing 65% $1.85B, +16%; EMEA at 25% $715M, +28% on sports rights renewals like Premier League bundles; and APAC/Other at 10% $285M, +12% despite regulatory headwinds in India mirroring Jio's content pivot.

Our paid subscriber base expanded to 28.2 million globally, up 1.8 million net adds QoQ and 6.5 million YoY—outpacing industry averages of 4-5% growth per company filings from Roku and Magna. Total paid subs 28.2M, up 28% YoY driven by bundling with our 5G mobile plans 40% of adds; net adds 1.8M, +20% QoQ with U.S. +1.1M, EMEA +0.5M, APAC +0.2M; blended ARPU $13.25, +2% with premium tier $16.99 at 55% mix and ad-tier uplift from 20% more impressions; monthly churn 1.8%, -10% QoQ best-in-class vs. Hulu's 2.2% with AI recs reducing churn 15% via 85% content match rate; SVOD penetration 72%, +2 pts with free-to-paid conversion at 28% boosted by trials tied to FWA broadband.

Regionally, U.S. ARPU held firm at $14.50 amid price hikes mirroring Comcast's strategy, while EMEA grew 5% to €11.80 on UEFA content. APAC lagged at $8.20 due to price sensitivity, but we're addressing via localized Hindi/Tamil originals.

Profitability scaled impressively, with adjusted EBITDA of $785 million—27.5% margin, expanding 450 basis points YoY from 23% and 200 bps QoQ. This reflects operating leverage from fixed content costs amortized over larger sub base amortization now 18% of revenue vs. 22% YoY; 15% reduction in acquisition costs per sub via telco channel down to $45 vs. $55 industry avg per Antenna data; EBITDA excludes $120M in one-time sports rights acceleration, normalizing to 30% margin. Free cash flow contribution hit $450 million, funding our $2B annual content capex slate, including 50 new originals and live sports like NFL Sunday Ticket-style packages.

Performance was propelled by technical edge: Rolled out 5G-optimized low-latency streaming under 5s via edge CDN partnerships with Akamai and our own MEC nodes, reducing buffering 40%—critical for live events, where we grew 35% YoY. AI personalization, powered by our 'TeleAI' engine similar to Netflix's recs but telco-data infused, drove 25% higher engagement and 18% LTV uplift.

Regional momentum: U.S. strength from bundling with 85M wireless postpaid lines 65% attach rate; EMEA sports surge post-DAZN tie-up; APAC via Jio-like super-app integration in Indonesia and Philippines, targeting 10M subs by FY25. Strategic moves: Launched ad-tier globally, adding $200M ARR run-rate; acquired boutique studio PixelForge for $300M to bolster unscripted content e.g., reality TV competing with ITV Studios; and expanded FAST channels to 50, mimicking Pluto TV's 500M hours/month playbook.

Looking ahead, we guide Q4 segment revenue growth of 16-18% YoY, with subs +1.7-1.9M and margins +100 bps to 28.5%. Risks include content cost inflation Hollywood strikes echo and ad market softness, but our telco moat—bundling 20% cheaper than standalone—positions us for 15%+ CAGR through 2027, outpacing Magna's 12% forecast for converged media.

Good afternoon, everyone. I'd like to dive deeper into our ARPU dynamics, which continue to be a cornerstone of our revenue growth story here at TeleMedia Corp. As you know, blended ARPU—our key metric across mobile, broadband, and media services—reached $58.42 in Q3, marking a robust 5.2% year-over-year increase from $55.51 last year. This $2.91 sequential uplift reflects the disciplined execution of our pricing architecture and bundling initiatives, which have offset macroeconomic headwinds like inflation-driven churn in prepaid segments and competitive intensity in select markets.

Mobile postpaid ARPU: $49.27, +4.8% YoY $2.25 increase. Postpaid mobile remains our highest-margin ARPU driver, benefiting from targeted pricing resets and premium 5G plan migrations. In Q3, we implemented modest 3-5% price increases on our Unlimited Plus and Ultra plans—mirroring moves by peers like Verizon and T-Mobile—capturing $1.20 of the YoY lift. These hikes were phased regionally: full implementation in North America, where 78% of our postpaid base now subscribes to 5G plans averaging $52 ARPU, up from 62% a year ago.

Bundling has been transformative here, with our '5G Home + Stream' package—pairing mmWave 5G mobile with ad-supported Paramount+ and our proprietary TeleMedia Sports Pass—driving 12% attachment rates, adding $4.50/month in ancillary revenue per bundled sub. This mirrors the success of AT&T's WarnerMedia bundles pre-spin but with higher stickiness due to our integrated 5G Standalone core network, which enables low-latency streaming. Penetration hit 22% in urban markets like the Northeast U.S., contributing 1.8pp to the YoY ARPU growth. Prepaid mobile ARPU ticked up modestly to $28.15, +2.1% YoY, held back by promotional discounting to counter MVNO pressure from Mint Mobile and Visible. However, our AI-driven dynamic pricing engine—leveraging real-time elasticity models—optimized promo depth, limiting erosion to just 0.5pp.

Fixed broadband and converged ARPU: $76.84, +7.1% YoY $5.39 increase. Broadband is the star performer, fueled by our aggressive fiber-to-the-premises FTTP rollout and fixed wireless access expansion. GPON and XGS-PON deployments reached 45% of our footprint, enabling 1Gbps+ speeds that justify premium pricing—our 1Gig plan now averages $92/month, up 6% YoY.

Bundling shines brightest here: 65% of new broadband adds took our 'Fiber Quad Play'—fiber internet, mobile, linear TV, and Netflix/Disney+ Bundle—for an effective ARPU of $112, versus $85 for standalone broadband. This strategy, akin to Comcast's Xfinity StreamSaver but with deeper media integration via our owned TeleMedia+ SVOD platform, boosted cross-sell by 18% YoY. In Europe, where regulatory caps on copper sunset have opened pricing windows, our UK and German fiber bundles lifted regional ARPU +9.2% to €68 $74 equivalent, outpacing BT Group's 4% gain. FWA ARPU grew even faster at +11.3% to $62, as we targeted rural underpenetrated areas with 5G FWA kits bundled to mobile lines—adding 250K subs and $8M in quarterly revenue. This is accretive at 2x EBITDA margins, helping offset DOCSIS 3.1 upgrade costs.

Media and entertainment ARPU: $14.62, +3.9% YoY $0.55 increase. Our media overlay—35% of total households—saw ARPU expansion from targeted ad-tier upsells and sports rights leverage. The 'Sports+ Premium' bundle, featuring NFL Sunday Ticket parity and UEFA Champions League streaming, added $7/month at 15% take-rate, directly competing with YouTube TV's pricing. Churn here was sub-1%, thanks to our zero-rating of TeleMedia+ data on mobile plans.

Regionally: North America 72% of subs +5.8% YoY blended ARPU to $60.10, driven by 5G fixed-mobile convergence and minimal regulatory drag. California and Texas fiber pricing held firm despite Spectrum's aggressive promos. Europe 18% +4.1% to $52 equivalent, tempered by Ofcom/Vodafone merger scrutiny but lifted by Italian FTTH bundles post-Open Fiber JV. Latin America and APAC 10% +6.7% to $38 equivalent, with Brazil's prepaid-to-postpaid shifts and India's Jio-like bundling of 5G with regional content fueling growth, though FX headwinds shaved 1pp.

These ARPU gains stem from our 'Revenue Quality Framework': data-led pricing analytics predicting 92% elasticity compliance, bundling algorithms targeting 25% household quad-play penetration by year-end, and capex-efficient 5G/FTTH scale. We've captured 70% pricing power pass-through amid 4.5% CPI inflation, with net pricing up 4.2% YoY excluding promos.

Looking forward, we guide Q4 blended ARPU to $59.10-$59.50 +5-5.5% YoY, assuming continued 5G adoption target 85% postpaid and new bundles like Apple TV+ integration. Risks include potential EU DMA pricing constraints, but our owned IP and spectrum position 1.8GHz midband nationwide provide a moat. This ARPU trajectory supports our full-year revenue growth reaffirmation at 6-7% and EBITDA margins expanding 150bps to 42%.

Thank you, Alex. I'll now turn to our Enterprise and B2B segment, which continues to be a cornerstone of our growth strategy in the Telecommunications and Media landscape. As you know, this segment leverages our world-class 5G network, edge computing capabilities, and media delivery platforms to address the surging demand for secure, low-latency connectivity and data-intensive applications amid digital transformation and AI adoption. In Q3, Enterprise and B2B revenues reached $2.8 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter, outpacing our overall company growth and the broader industry average of 12% as reported by Dell'Oro Group. Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded to 42%, a 300-basis-point improvement, driven by higher-margin managed services and recurring SaaS revenue streams, which now comprise 65% of the segment—up from 55% a year ago.

First, 5G Private Networks and Network Slicing: Our crown jewel for industrial IoT and mission-critical use cases. We've seen explosive traction here, fueled by manufacturing reshoring and smart factory deployments. Total 5G Enterprise contracts signed YTD now exceed $1.2 billion, a 25% increase from the prior year. A key win was our $450 million, 5-year deal with Global Auto Manufacturer akin to Ford/GM, deploying private 5G across 15 U.S. plants for real-time AR/VR quality control and AGV orchestration. This builds on our Q2 $320 million expansion with similar to Procter & Gamble, enhancing supply chain visibility via CBRS-integrated slicing. Regionally, North America accounts for 60% of deployments, but APAC is accelerating—our $180 million partnership with a leading Singaporean logistics firm mirrors the momentum we're seeing in ASEAN, where 5G spectrum auctions have unlocked brownfield upgrades. Technically, our ORAN-compliant slicing platform delivers 99.9999% uptime, with latency under 5ms, positioning us ahead of competitors like Ericsson and Nokia in TCO metrics.

Second, Multi-Access Edge Computing MEC and Hybrid Cloud Connectivity: Capitalizing on AI/ML workloads. Edge revenues grew 22% YoY to $850 million, as enterprises migrate from hyperscalers like AWS Outposts to our telco-grade MEC for reduced egress fees and sovereign data compliance. We've integrated our MEC with NVIDIA's AI Enterprise stack, enabling on-prem inference at scale. A marquee win: $280 million multi-year agreement with Major U.S. Healthcare Network like Kaiser Permanente for edge-enabled telemedicine and predictive analytics across 50 hospitals, slashing data transit costs by 40%. In EMEA, regulatory tailwinds from the EU Data Act have boosted our pipeline; we just inked a €150 million ~$165 million deal with a German automotive Tier-1 supplier for V2X edge orchestration. Our MEC fabric now spans 1,200 points of presence, with uCPE deployments up 30%, driving ARPU uplift of 15% through SD-WAN bundling.

Third, Cybersecurity and Secure Access Service Edge SASE: Defending against rising threats in a zero-trust world. This high-margin pillar hit $650 million in Q3 revenues, +28% YoY, as ransomware attacks surged 35% per Verizon's DBIR. Our SASE-as-a-Service, powered by our SSE fabric and integrated with Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange, has been a differentiator. Key win: $220 million, 3-year contract with Fortune 500 Retailer akin to Walmart, securing 5,000 stores with AI-driven threat detection and DEWA Distributed Edge Web Application Firewall. We've also expanded media-specific offerings, like our $95 million deal with a European broadcaster similar to BBC for secure CDN and anti-piracy DRM during live sports streaming peaks. Margins here are north of 50%, with churn under 2%, reflecting sticky adoption.

Media Enterprise Solutions: Bridging Telecom and Content Monetization. On the media front, our B2B ad tech and OTT platforms generated $420 million, up 16% YoY, amid CTV fragmentation. We've won $110 million in programmatic deals, including a $75 million pact with akin to Disney's ad sales arm for audience-matched DOOH inventory via our 5G-backhauled OOH network. Trends like retail media networks RMNs are tailwinds—our API integrations with Criteo's commerce media platform have doubled addressable spend in that vertical.

These wins reflect our "Network-to-Edge-to-Cloud" strategy, where we're not just a pipe but a full-stack partner, much like how Verizon's 5G Edge has disrupted AWS Direct Connect economics. Our $15 billion B2B pipeline is up 20% YoY, with 45% weighted towards multi-year contracts >$100 million. Risks include supply chain delays in ORAN radios, but our U.S. Manufacturing Fund mitigates this. Regionally, U.S. hyperscaler capex cuts are opportunity neutral—enterprises are reallocating to telco edge for 30-50% cost savings. Looking ahead, we guide to full-year Enterprise growth of 17-20%, with 5G contributing over half.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your plans for addressing the digital divide and ensuring that all communities have access to affordable broadband, and how do you plan to achieve 3 million FWA subscribers by year-end?

David Chen: Great question, Lisa. Addressing the digital divide is core to our mission.
